title: Terraform module for GPU capacity policy (ASG + Karpenter) in Private VPC
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Add a reusable Terraform module that codifies GPU capacity policies for Private VPC deployments. The module must support two autoscaling backends: EC2 Auto Scaling Groups (ASG) for predictable reserved pools and Karpenter for burst/spot. Goals: provide a single, documented interface for node group sizing, tenancy, instance selector constraints, taints/labels for runtime, health-check hooks, and upgrade-safe lifecycle handling. Must integrate with existing private VPC module layouts and respect customer-managed KMS and subnet mappings. Avoid duplicating existing launch templates; instead accept an optional launch_template_id or generate a minimal overlay. This work will also include integration tests and a migration plan for existing dedicated clusters.
acceptance_criteria: Terraform module exposes variables for instance_type_preferences, min_capacity, max_capacity, priority_profile (reserved|burstable), taints_and_labels, node_ami_id, and lifecycle_hooks
Module can deploy both ASG-backed and Karpenter-backed nodegroups via a single boolean switch and documented examples
Rolling upgrade strategy that drains GPU workloads via cordon/drain hooks and respects eviction timeouts is implemented
End-to-end integration test in staging that provisions a small GPU cluster in Private VPC and demonstrates node addition/removal under load
Documentation and migration guide published to Confluence; sample PR for customer repo included
comments: 2025-11-04 Lucas Moreno: spike completed on instance selector constraints. Karpenter provisioning of p5d-like families works but needs explicit capacity type mapping for on-demand vs spot.
2025-11-06 Review (PM: Jonah Reed): prefer explicit taint/label schema to avoid accidental scheduling. Add example for mixed instance types in docs.
2025-11-11 Design review (Infra): decided to accept external launch_template_id to support existing customer overrides rather than regenerating full templates.
2025-11-15 QA: integration test flakes when ASG scale-in triggers while GPU pods are terminating. Added preDrain hook and extended eviction timeout in test manifest.
2025-11-18 Security: require KMS key ARN input when enable_encryption is true. Added validation to module variables.
migration_plan: Phase 1: Deploy module with ASG example into staging and run workload tests. Phase 2: Offer Karpenter flag in staging to validate burst behavior. Phase 3: Coordinate with two pilot customers to toggle module in their Private VPCs during maintenance window. Phase 4: Gradual roll-forward by converting existing nodegroups to managed by module while keeping previous launch templates until verification. Each step requires a rollback checkpoint and an automated snapshot of launch template + ASG config.
rollback_strategy: If a deploy causes pod disruption > accepted threshold, revert Terraform to previous state using statefile snapshot, restore original launch_template_id on ASG, and scale-up replacement nodes. For Karpenter changes, disable provisioner and recreate previous nodegroup with previous taints/labels. Automate alerting with runbook for SRE.
health_checks: Node-level: EC2 status checks and a DaemonSet that reports GPU driver + CUDA health to /healthz
ASG: lifecycle hook that runs preDrain script; CloudWatch alarm on scale-in frequency
Karpenter: provisioner metrics for pending pods and pod scheduling latency; webhook to block provisioning if driver mismatch detected
Application-level: readiness probes for GPU jobs and Prometheus rules for long-running eviction events
test_plan: Unit: terraform validate and module unit tests for variable validation
Integration: deploy full module into a temporary Private VPC in staging, run GPU workload harness (small batch training + inference) to trigger scaling
Chaos: simulate node termination during GPU pod eviction to ensure preDrain hooks and rollback behave as expected
Performance: measure cold-start time for Karpenter provisioned GPU nodes vs. ASG warm pool
monitoring_dashboards: Datadog: Private-GPU-Nodegroups overview (cpu/gpu utilization, pending pods, scale events)
Prometheus: Karpenter provisioner metrics and ASG scaling activity
Grafana: upgrade-safe drain timeline visualization for recent rollouts
risk_and_mitigations: Risk: Spot interruptions with Karpenter could cause model training job failures. Mitigation: explicit capacity profile preference and safe eviction hooks that checkpoint work when possible.
Risk: Incorrect taints/labels could block scheduling and cause SLOs to breach. Mitigation: schema validation and example manifests in docs.
Risk: Terraform state drift between generated launch templates and customer-managed templates. Mitigation: accept launch_template_id as input and treat module as non-destructive by default.
